segments.he: הרב ר' שניאור זלמן שמע מהמגיד הגדול זצ"ל אמר לו שמי שלומד שלא לשמה שוכח את זה האביי ורבא שבגמרא ותפס איזה אביי ורבא ואח"כ נזדמן שבא הרב למקום של מתנגדים והי' שם א' גדול שלהם ואמר שהוא יראה להחסיד שאינו יכול ללמוד. ושאל אותו כמה אביי ורבא יש בכל הש"ס אמר לו הרב ואתם יודעים ענה ואמר כן והתחיל לזרוק מפיו פה יש אביי ורבא ופה וכן הזכיר כל אביי ורבא שיש בש"ס מלבד זה אביי ורבא שהמגיד אמר לו שמי שלומד שלא לשמה שוכח זה אביי ורבא. זה לא הזכיר, ושאל אותו הרב יותר לא יש ענה ואמר לא ענה הרב ואמר הלא יש זה האביי ורבא (הנ"ל) ונעשה פניו כשולי קדרה. ענה הרב תאמר לאנשים שעברו שם אל תחשבו שאני יודע זה יותר היינו כל האביי ורבא רק מקובלני מפי המגיד ז"ל שמי שלומד שלא לשמה שוכח זה האביי ורבא ע''כ כשהזכיר כל האביי ורבא וזה האביי ורבא לא הזכיר נזכר בדברי המגיד ז''ל הנ''ל
segments.en:
Reb Nachman the grandson of Moharan'as said: "Can we understand the mercy of Hashem?" — for these are the ways of G-d that cannot be understood by our physical reasoning. For we see many times, G-d preserve us, that a body is being carried and after the bier walk many orphans — large and small — weeping and crying, and they say "Kel maleh rachamim" [G-d full of mercy] and invoke the mercy of Hashem. And by our coarse reasoning — is this the mercy? Yet certainly this is the primary mercy — Hashem knows how to show mercy. [And yet, Rabbainu already taught us that we must beseech Hashem: "El Shaddai give you mercy" — as Yaakov Avinu prayed — meaning: hand over the mercy to us, so that we too might understand the mercy, not only He in His eyes. Let everyone understand and see the mercy plainly — meaning: children, life, and sustenance. See Likutay Moharan Part II, chapter 67.]

Rabbainu told a story that the Ba'al Shem Tov had told — about a certain poritz who had a Jewish innkeeper who had held his lease for a long time. Then a time came when he could not pay his rent, and the poritz placed the Jew and his household in a pit, and so forth. And this poritz had no children at all. And specifically after this terrible event, a son was born to the poritz. This is the matter of the justification of Divine judgment — "Your righteousness is like the mountains of G-d; Your judgments are a great deep" — meaning: even though Your judgments are a great deep [the just judgment of Hashem is not seen with the eye, and it appears that the judgment is buried and hidden to the depths of the great deep] — nonetheless we must know and believe that "Your righteousness is like the mountains of G-d" — that in this very matter Your righteousness is as the mountains of G-d — very great — and His mercy is very great, and everything is in justice and uprightness by what we do not understand greatly. Yet one must never, ever reflect negatively about Hashem, for "all His paths are faithfulness, and there is no iniquity — righteous and upright is He."

And Rabbainu said that the matter of the Rosh HaShanah gathering at his grave is very great and very beloved in his eyes — and he said that even from the Heichal Ken Tzipor in Gan Eden [the palace of Mashiach — the highest of all the palaces] he would come to the gathering on Rosh HaShanah to pray together with them. [Just as we see that Hashem Himself leaves all the upper worlds and praises His Shechinah among those below — in the aspect of "and You are holy, enthroned upon the praises of Israel" — and "the Tzaddikim are found more in death than in life."] Rabbainu also said again how the Hidden Book is great and the Burnt Book is great — but to be with him on Rosh HaShanah is even greater. [For Rabbainu had already said that there is nothing greater than this: "There is nothing greater than this!" — as printed in Chayay Moharan, see there.]
